newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman describes Plains wheat damage area.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman describes Plains wheat damage area.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the greatest freeze damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop appeared to be in the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles and south of Interstate 70 in Kansas.

Glickman discussed the week-ago freeze in general terms during an appearance at the National Association of Agrcultural Journalists meeting. He was in Kansas last weekend and spoke to a crop-condition expert.
"We have not analyzed the full extent of freeze damage," he told the group but it appeared there was little or no damage north of I-70.
The largest area of damage, he said, was in southwestern Kansas, the Texas panhandle and the Oklahoma panhandle.
There was some damage between I-70 and Highway 54 in Kansas, he said.
